game.title: Alan Wake
game.notes: 32-bit exe (AlanWake.exe, PE machine=0x14C). Ships a from-scratch d3d9.dll forwarding proxy in this project (exports exactly Direct3DCreate9, no hook code as of 2026-09-03).

api_notes: Window title is exactly 'Alan Wake - v<version>' (version string embedded, changes per patch - match on 'Alan Wake' substring, not the full title).
SendInput scancode keyboard + relative mouse work for basic capture/focus operations; menu navigation not yet mapped (Esc tried once, inconclusive - see hazards).

2026-09-05 (home PC): SendInput with SCANCODES did NOT reach this game (Space at the title, twice, once held 0.25 s: nothing); the same keys as VIRTUAL-KEY events (wVk, no scancode flag) worked at once. The dev PC record of 2026-09-04 says scancodes worked there - n=1 each way, so try VK first and fall back. Driver: alan-wake-vr/dev-archive/tools/awdrive.py (+ the awvk helper in the notes).

2026-09-08 (dev PC), SUPERSEDES the two n=1 records above as the operating rule: a BARE keypress does not reach this game at all - neither VK nor scancode - even with the game window verified as the foreground window. A LEFT MOUSE CLICK INSIDE THE WINDOW IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THE KEY makes it land, and the effect does NOT persist: the next key needs its own click. Rule: click, key, click, key. Measured on the MAIN MENU (a stable state that does not auto-advance, so every result is attributable), n=2 each: VK alone no; scancode alone no; cursor moved inside the window without clicking then VK no; click then VK YES; VK again without a new click no. Same rule in gameplay: 2.5 s of W with no click was indistinguishable from the no-input control (mean luma delta 2.87 vs 2.92); a click then 3 s of W walked the character visibly. WHY the click is needed is NOT established - plausibly each external shell command steals foreground and the game never receives a proper activation back. The earlier records are kept, not deleted: the missing ingredient in both may simply have been the click. Driver: alan-wake-vr/dev-archive/tools/awkeys.py

2026-09-08 DISPROVED, and it nearly became a finding: 'VK events work here, scancodes do not'. The title screen advanced right after a VK space, but a no-input control then showed the TITLE AUTO-ADVANCES INTO AN ATTRACT REEL ON ITS OWN (60 s of no input, never the title), so every transition attributed to a keypress was equally explained by the attract timeout. Never test input on the title screen of this game; use the main menu, which is stable.

states.name: gameplay
states.detect: Third-person over-shoulder view, objective text + flashlight-battery dial HUD top-left, continuous non-zero frame delta via BitBlt capture.

states.name: minimized (fullscreen-exclusive focus-loss)
states.detect: GetWindowRect returns the Windows sentinel (-32000,-32000)-(-31840,-31972); IsIconic() == True. BitBlt capture at the window's client origin returns a near-black/tiny image even though the process is alive and CPU/GPU-active.
states.notes: See hazards: this build auto-minimizes on ANY external focus steal while running D3D9 exclusive fullscreen (resolution.xml fullscreen=1). Fix: ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_RESTORE) then SetForegroundWindow - confirmed twice to fully recover the running session with no state loss (same scene, same HUD, same character position both times).

states.name: title
states.detect: ALAN WAKE logo over a foggy forest; 'Press any key to play' (takes Space); Nitro/Remedy credits and version at the bottom.

states.name: main_menu
states.detect: Lighthouse scene; vertical list Continue Game / New Game / Episodes / Options / Extras / Quit; 'Select' prompt bottom-right.

states.name: difficulty
states.detect: 'Difficulty' label with Easy / Normal / Nightmare over the lighthouse; reached from New Game.

states.name: load_game_slots
states.detect: 'Load Game' label with numbered slots ('1: Steam Cloud Alan Wake'); reached from Continue Game once a save exists.

states.name: pause_menu
states.detect: Resume Game / Restart Checkpoint / Manuscript / Options / Statistics / Quit To Menu over the blurred scene; footer 'Esc Back  Enter Select'. Esc during a video also opens it (does not skip the video); Esc again resumes.

states.name: video_playback
states.detect: Letterboxed fly-over / studio logos; the proxy log shows only c0+4 / c0+5 constant uploads (~200/s). The title's forest and the lighthouse main menu are ALSO video, not 3D: a live projection matrix only exists in the studio logos before the title and in the in-engine intro after the fly-over.

states.name: attract_reel
states.detect: Letterboxed cinematic clips (Bright Falls fly-over, Alan close-ups) cycling with the title card, with only c0+4 / c0+5 vertex-constant uploads in the proxy log.
states.notes: Entered from the title with NO input after roughly 20 s and cycles back through the title. This is why the title is useless for testing input.

states.name: developer_menu
states.detect: Header 'Developer Menu' at the left with four rows: Get Lots of Guns, Get Flashlight and Batteries, Unlock all Episodes (Easy and Normal), Unlock Nightmare difficulty. Only reachable when the game was started with -developermenu.
states.notes: A QA unlock menu - nothing for camera, stereo or debug rendering. All four entries alter save/profile state, so do not select them; Esc backs out.

steps: wait for the window (windowed if resolution.xml fullscreen=0)
click inside the window, then send space - repeat about 6 times (awkeys.py --repeat 6 space)
capture and verify the menu list before pressing anything: Continue Game is highlighted
routes.notes: Rewritten 2026-09-08: the old 'press Space at the title' step is not sufficient on its own, because a bare keypress does not reach this game (see input.api_notes). The title also auto-advances into an attract reel, so do not treat reaching the menu as proof a key landed.

steps: Down x5 to Quit - VERIFY the highlight
'Are you sure you want to Quit?' - Enter accepts (Esc cancels)
process exits to desktop in a few seconds
routes.notes: Reached from gameplay via Esc to the pause menu then to the main menu (pause route not exercised 2026-09-04).

steps: Down x1 -> New Game (verify the highlight)
Enter -> fly-over video (~60 s) then the in-engine intro; Esc pauses, Esc resumes
Enter on Continue Game -> Load Game slot list
Enter on slot 1 -> load (~30 s) -> the checkpoint's video/cutscene, then gameplay
routes.notes: An Enter sent within ~5 s of the title->menu transition is eaten (twice). Capture-verify the main menu before pressing.

steps: Esc -> pause menu, Resume Game highlighted
Enter -> 'Are you sure you want to Quit?' -> Enter
main menu, Continue Game highlighted (~8 s)
Enter -> confirm -> Enter; process exits within 2 s, proxy hooks unwound in order
routes.notes: Proven twice on 2026-09-05. This is the graceful route; WM_CLOSE is no longer needed.

resolution.xml.purpose: width/height/fullscreen. Read at process start only - editing it while the game is running has no live effect; takes effect on the NEXT launch.
resolution.xml.notes: 2026-09-08: set to 1280x720 windowed on the dev PC so the game does NOT fill the screen - at 1920x1080 windowed on a 1920x1080 monitor it covered everything. Read at process start only, so edit it while the game is closed. Previous value kept as resolution.xml.bak-2026-09-08-was-1920x1080. IMPORTANT: the BACKBUFFER aspect, not the monitor, is what the camera signature is keyed on - so pinning a 16:9 windowed size makes MatchXS/MatchYS portable between the dev PC (16:9 monitor) and the home PC (21:9 monitor). Fullscreen on the home PC would give ys/xs ~2.37 and need a re-measure.

documented_launch_flags._measured_2026_09_08: THE COMPLETE LIST, read out of AlanWake.exe's own option table beside the format string 'Unknown command line option "%s"'. This supersedes the earlier [reported] wiki list: shaders, SENSSCALE=/sensscale=, GPUCOUNT=/gpucount=, freecamera, directaiming, nativekeys, rigidcamera, showfps, verbose, developermenu, largeshadowmaps, noblur, forcesurround, forcestereo, cleanaccount, cleancloud, novsync, nosound, window, LOCALE=/locale=. NOTE -w <n> and -h <n> are NOT in the table; width/height come from resolution.xml.
documented_launch_flags._DANGER: NEVER pass cleanaccount or cleancloud. They are in the same table and the names say they wipe local account state and Steam Cloud data. Nothing has been run to find out what they do and nothing should be - the project's save is the test fixture.
documented_launch_flags.-developermenu: [verified-live 2026-09-08] Works. Adds a '[Developer Menu]' row to the main menu (between Extras and Quit) AND to the pause menu (between Statistics and Quit To Menu). Contents are only: Get Lots of Guns, Get Flashlight and Batteries (both greyed at the main menu, in-game only), Unlock all Episodes (Easy and Normal), Unlock Nightmare difficulty. It is a QA unlock menu - no stereo entries, no camera/FOV/debug toggles, no console. All four items alter save/profile state; do not select them.
documented_launch_flags.-rigidcamera: [measured 2026-09-08, treatment half only] Accepted without error. With it armed, walking produced ZERO per-frame vertical camera shift across 13 frame pairs (estimator validated against injected +/-1, +/-3, +/-8 px offsets). NOT established that the flag caused this - no no-flag control has been run at the same save point yet.
documented_launch_flags.-noblur: [untested] Accepted without error in the same run; no observation was made.
documented_launch_flags.-freecamera: [reported] a real, official free-camera tool, controller-driven, right-thumbstick toggle - no confirmed keyboard/mouse equivalent. Confirmed present in the binary's option table 2026-09-08; still not tested live.
documented_launch_flags.-window / -novsync / -showfps / -senssca: [measured 2026-09-08] present in the binary's option table; behaviour untested.

entry_points.steam_app_id: 108710 (start steam://rungameid/108710). On a fresh install Steam first runs a ~7 s first-run setup that shows in content_log.txt as App Running and exits; the game starts on the SECOND launch attempt (2026-09-05).

commands.console: NONE. This game ships no console and no exec route was found; configuration reaches the mod through d3d9_proxy.ini, which is read at process start only, so every config change costs a relaunch. [verified-live 2026-09-08]

hazards.hazard: This build auto-minimizes on ANY external focus steal while D3D9-exclusive-fullscreen
hazards.notes: Reproduced twice, from two unrelated causes: (1) sending Alt+Enter - the ALT key alone generates WM_SYSKEYDOWN, which this build appears to treat as losing exclusive-mode focus; (2) merely launching an unrelated GUI application (x32dbg.exe) nearby, with no attach ever made. Both times GetWindowRect reported the Windows-minimized sentinel (-32000,-32000)-(-31840,-31972) and IsIconic()==True, and both times ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_RESTORE) + SetForegroundWindow fully recovered the exact running state with no loss (same scene, same HUD, same character position). DO NOT send Alt+Enter to this game live to try to toggle windowed mode - it does not toggle, it minimizes. Use resolution.xml + a relaunch instead (see entry_points.config_files).

hazards.hazard: A game-window close (WM_CLOSE) produced a Windows crash-report minidump, despite a fast, non-hanging process exit
hazards.notes: PostMessage(hwnd, WM_CLOSE, 0, 0) made the process leave the process list within ~4s with no visible hang - insufficient evidence to call it 'graceful', corrected in-session. A fresh minidump (15,718 bytes) appeared at the exact close time. NOTE for future sessions: that exact byte size also matches ONE of nine pre-existing dumps from an unrelated 2026-08-25 session (the other eight were 216-254 KB, a visibly different/larger fault), which hints this specific small dump may be a repeatable, likely-benign exception the shutdown path always trips - not proven, n=2. Do not copy dump FILE CONTENTS into any repo (a minidump is a memory snapshot that can contain the game's own compiled code/assets - treat it like any other original game file, never distribute it). Recording only size/timestamp metadata is fine. A verified in-game quit route (through a menu) is still unknown and would be worth finding before assuming WM_CLOSE is the best available method.

hazards.hazard: The x64dbg MCP automation bridge did not connect on this machine
hazards.notes: SYMPTOM UNCHANGED: start_session reported a timeout even though x32dbg.exe did launch and run standalone, and list_sessions never showed it. THE RECORDED CAUSE WAS WRONG and is corrected here (2026-09-07). It said six 'apparently-stale' x64dbg-automate-mcp.exe helpers suggested an estate-wide bridge issue. Measured 2026-09-07: five such helpers were running and EVERY ONE had a live claude parent process (five distinct, all alive), holding no TCP endpoints - they are one helper per open session, ordinary MCP behaviour, not leaked orphans. WHAT THE CONFIGURATION ACTUALLY IS: X64DBG_PATH (Process and User scope) points at ...\release\x96dbg.exe, which is x64dbg's LAUNCHER/SELECTOR, not a debugger - it picks x32 or x64 and starts it. The bridge resolves explicit parameter -> X64DBG_PATH -> shutil.which, then Popen()s that path and waits for a session to register, so if the process it launched is the selector, the handle it holds is not the debugger's: it waits, times out, and list_sessions stays empty while a perfectly good debugger runs. That is the symptom exactly. AND THERE ARE TWO INSTALLS, UNEVENLY PROVISIONED: the WinGet copy has x64dbg-automate.dp32 and .dp64; the AppData\Local\x64dbg copy has an EMPTY x32\plugins. Alan Wake is 32-bit, so it needs x32dbg AND the .dp32 - against the AppData copy a 32-bit session could never register.
candidate_causes: launcher indirection - the bridge holds the selector's handle, not the debugger's
half-provisioned install - a 32-bit session against the AppData copy has no automate plugin
contention between several sessions' helpers over the plugin's endpoint
hazards.how_to_separate_them: (1) vs (2): which install did the x32dbg.exe that launched come from? The WinGet copy has the .dp32; the AppData copy does not. (3): retry with only one Claude session open.
hazards.first_thing_to_try: Point X64DBG_PATH at the actual debugger binary matching the target's bitness - the WinGet install's x32\x32dbg.exe for this 32-bit game - or pass x64dbg_path explicitly to start_session, which the tool accepts per call. UNTESTED: nothing here has been run against a live session.

hazards.hazard: Proxy: a foreign hook layered on IDirect3D9 vtable slot 16 during the first (throwaway) load - most likely the Steam overlay - makes the second load chain into it and recurse CreateDevice until the process dies (~7 s, 1,669 calls in 1 ms). Timing-dependent: it happened once when the first block lived 700 ms, not on three launches where it lived 16 ms.
hazards.notes: Log tells: 'CreateDevice hook: slot 16 holds ..., not ours' at the first unload, then a burst of 'IDirect3D9::CreateDevice called'. Queued fix: never chain into a foreign slot-16 pointer.

hazards.hazard: A small (~15.7 KB) crash minidump appears in Documents\Remedy\AlanWake at every clean menu quit, with the proxy hooks already removed (n=3: 15,718 / 15,666 B). Benign shutdown-path exception; not ours. Do not commit dump contents.
Pre-creating Documents\Remedy\AlanWakeesolution.xml with fullscreen=0 on a never-run install works: the game came up windowed 1920x1080 on its first real launch, no minimise events in four launches.
IDirect3D9 vtable slot 16 is ALWAYS already hooked on a Steam machine - a d3d9 proxy that patches it cannot install
hazards.notes: Two launches, four proxy loads, every one refused: slot 16 held a pointer owned by Steam\gameoverlayrenderer.dll (load 1 of both launches) and by C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\apphelp.dll (load 2 of the direct launch), never by the real d3d9.dll. A vtable is shared per class, so the owner CHANGED between two loads 350 ms apart in one process; why is not established. The fix is to stop patching the vtable and return your own COM object from Direct3DCreate9, which the game calls directly when you are the proxy.

hazards.hazard: Launching AlanWake.exe DIRECTLY does not avoid the Steam overlay
hazards.notes: Bypassing the Steam launcher (SteamAppId in the environment, Start-Process on the exe) still had gameoverlayrenderer.dll owning slot 16 on the first proxy load. With Steam running the overlay is injected regardless, so this is not a way around it. n=1.

hazards.name: the activation click can select a menu item
hazards.detail: Because every key needs a preceding mouse click, the click position matters: the menu list occupies the lower third of the window, so a click there SELECTS an item. The main menu's 'Quit' and the pause menu's 'Restart Checkpoint' are both reachable this way. awkeys.py clicks at 15% of window height for this reason. Always capture-verify the highlight before Enter; never blind key-count past a destructive item.

hazards.name: -developermenu shifts every menu index by one
hazards.detail: The flag inserts a '[Developer Menu]' row into BOTH the main menu (between Extras and Quit) and the pause menu (between Statistics and Quit To Menu). So Quit becomes Down x6 instead of Down x5, and Quit To Menu likewise. Any recorded key-count route is off by one while the flag is set. Capture and verify the highlight rather than counting.

notes: 2026-09-04b: the FreeLibrary-at-detach fix is confirmed live - the proxy's second d3d9 load now stays resident and the game renders through it (title + main menu). The proxy owns the real device. [verified-live 2026-09-04]

2026-09-05: handedness read live - g_mViewToClip is LEFT-handed (clip.w = +view.z), stored with registers as rows of a column-vector matrix (+1 at storage index 14). Main camera at c192 in skinned shaders (16:9, near 0.2, far 1000). The engine uploads constants as whole 128-register blocks (c0+128, c128+128). See the alan-wake-vr dossier 4c.
